subject: Biology
title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants - DPP 07 (Double Fertilization & Endosperm)

questions.question: After triple fusion central cell changes into–
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct: Primary endosperm cell (PEC).

questions.question: A fertilised egg of a plant has 40 chromosomes. The number of chromosomes present in the microspore mother cell are
Double fertilisation is fusion of:
options: Two eggs and polar nuclei with pollen nuclei
One male gamete with egg and other with synergid
One male gamete with egg and other with two secondary nucleus
questions.explanation: Option (D) is correct: One male gamete with egg and other with two secondary nucleus.

questions.question: Double fertilisation is:
options: Fusion of two male gametes of a pollen tube with two different eggs
Fusion of one male gamete with two polar nuclei
Fusion of two male gametes with one egg
questions.explanation: Option (D) is correct: Syngamy and triple fusion.

questions.question: In angiosperms, triple fusion produces:
questions.explanation: Option (C) is correct: Primary endospermic nucleus.

questions.question: The central cell after triple fusion becomes the:
questions.explanation: Option (A) is correct: PEC (primary endosperm cell).

questions.question: In the formation of endosperm of wheat, which of the following cell is involved?
The correct sequence of embryogeny in dicots is
options: Zygote Proembryo Globular Heart- shaped Mature embryo
Zygote Globular Proembryo Heart- shaped Mature embryo
Zygote Proembryo Heart-shaped Globular Mature embryo
Zygote Globular Heart-shaped Proembryo Mature embryo
questions.explanation: Option (A) is correct: Zygote Proembryo Globular Heart- shaped Mature embryo.

questions.question: Go through the given diagram of a typical dicot embryo. In which of the following all the 3 parts labelled as A, B, C with their respective functions are correctly identifies?
options: A-Plumule, shoot system formation, B-Radicle, root system formation,C-Hypophysis, formation of radicle
A-Plumule, shoot system formation, B-Radicle, root system formation, C-Cotyledon, food storage
A-Radicle, root system formation, B-Plumule, shoot system formation, C-Cotyledon, food storage
A-Radicle, root system formation, B-Plumule, shoot system formation, C-Endosperm, food
questions.explanation: Option (B) is correct: A-Plumule, shoot system formation, B-Radicle, root system formation, C-Cotyledon, food storage.

questions.question: In which one of the options all the four parts A, B, C and D are correct?
options: A- Scutellum, B-Coleoptile, C-Radicle, D- Coleorhiza
A- Scutellum, B-Coleorhiza, C-Radicle, D- Coleoptile
A- Hypophysis, B-Coleorhiza, C-Radicle, D- Coleoptile
A- Hypophysis, B-Coleoptile, C-Radicle, D- Coleorhiza
questions.explanation: Option (A) is correct: A- Scutellum, B-Coleoptile, C-Radicle, D- Coleorhiza.

questions.question: Coleorrhiza is present at
options: Radical end enclosed the undifferential sheath
Shoot end enclosed the undifferential sheath
Root end enclosed the differential sheath
Shoot end enclosed the differential sheath

questions.question: Which of the given statements are true? (i) During the development of a dicot embryo heart shaped embryo is followed by globular enlarge. (ii) The part of the embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is epicotyl while the part below the level of cotyledons is hypocotyl. (iii) Monocot seeds possess a single cotyledon represented by scutellum.
